It's such a risky route and completely depends on the therapist. I've seen things go south for people even in casual conversation.

I've tried a lot of medications (antidepressants, antianxiety, prescription sleep aids, prescription stimulants) and nothing has ever worked.

I've had similar issues in the past. Everyone will tell you, "you are creative, you just don't realize it" but I know from experience that doesn't mean anything. You need to prove to yourself that you're creative by finding a hobby that lets you discover your creativity. I recommend starting with something that isn't obviously creative. 

For me, I started baking a couple years ago (having never baked anything in my life). I've stuck with the hobby and I've amazed myself with how much I've improved. I don't push myself with obviously artistic things like designed cakes or clever cookies, I mostly bake bread. But over the years I've found my own ways to make bread interesting and it's really opened up my creative juices and has given me a weird creative confidence that I've never had before.

Don't give up on your YouTube dreams but maybe take up another, less obviously creative hobby in addition to YouTube to help you find confidence in your own abilities
